items.title: Jon-Erik Kellso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: I started sort of going backwards from there and learning about and listening to Bix Beiderbecke and Louis Armstrong... I’ve had some students... go back and listen to Louis Armstrong and listen to the greats throughout history.

ctx.x: How did you get into the improvising end of things? © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

Well I got interested in that pretty early, because like I said I started playing when I was ten and right around the same time I was getting interested in my parents’ old records. And you know I asked my Dad about what’s going on — what is this? You know I wanted to know more about what was happening, and he’d explain to me when things were written out when things were just guys “taking a ride” as he liked to call it you know. And so I got interested in that and my friend Mike Karoub and I, like I said, we were…
Can you recall what Louis Armstrong you first heard? Which part of his career?
